1.title: Initial request
1.text:
The first request already contains three system blocks, a system message and our own prompt, in which we ask Claude to do something with computer use. The first message is the prompt, preceded by three reminders added by the harness: the user's email, commit attribution rules, and a note about the scratch folder. The second message has role system and is 34k characters long. It describes the environment and contains each MCP server's instructions, including a 6k-character section on computer use.

The computer-use tools are not loaded at first; their names appear only in a list of deferred tools. Claude's first action is to load the definitions of those tools and the computer-use skill.

comments.safeguards: Anthropic checks the model's tool calls; the response returns a verdict per call, for every call except ToolSearch in this session
comments.tools: No computer-use tools yet; they're deferred
comments.messages[0]: Just irrelevant instructions, then the prompt
comments.messages[0].content[3]: User asks for a calculation in the Calculator app
comments.messages[1]: Additional mid-conversation system message with descriptions of the MCP servers, one of which is the computer-use server

more: The model sees only the MCP tool names until it requests the tools. Sending all schemas in every request would add thousands of tokens to each call, while most sessions don't need these beefy tool descriptions because they don't use the computer.

2.title: Tool definitions added
2.text: Now we see the regular Claude API loop: the model asks for tools to be run, and the harness runs them, one iteration after another.

comments.tools: Harness adds the definitions of the computer-use tools
comments.messages[2].content[0]: Reasoning isn't in the log; the API returns only an encrypted signature, removed here
comments.messages[2].content[1]: Model creates a todo list that you see in the interface; the same tool updates the task status later
comments.messages[2].content[2]: Model asks to load the computer-use skill
comments.messages[2].content[3]: Model asks for the computer-use tool definitions
comments.messages[3].content[0]: Harness confirms the todo list is shown
comments.messages[3].content[2]: Harness makes the computer-use tools callable and gives their descriptions
comments.messages[3].content[3]: Harness adds the skill's text: how to use the computer
comments.messages[3].content[4]: Harness confirms the tools are loaded

more: Once the model asks to load the deferred tools, the request's tools array has 27 new definitions, which the model can now choose from. A tool_reference block marks the point in the conversation where a definition becomes visible to the model. Before a reference appears, the model has only the tool names.

3.title: Access granted
3.text: Claude's first real computer-use call is request_access for Calculator. The user sees an approval dialog as a result of this call. The result is essentially "all good, you may proceed", and the MCP server records the grant, so from now on requests for this app are not blocked.

comments.messages[4].content[0]: Model requests approval for using Calculator app
comments.messages[5].content[0]: After approval, the harness returns that the use was approved
comments.messages[5].content[1]: Harness confirms the todo list update

4.title: open_application
4.text: Claude calls open_application. The result is again essentially "all good, it is already open".

comments.messages[6].content[0]: Model asks MCP server to open Calculator
comments.messages[7].content[0]: MCP server reports that Calculator is open and says which tools to use next

5.title: First screenshot
5.text: Claude calls app_screenshot. The result has three blocks: a 230×461 JPEG, a line that Claude Code adds after saving the image to disk, and the MCP server's text. The text gives the window id and an accessibility summary (the element list) with one line per clickable element: its number, role, box and title.

comments.messages[8].content[0]: Model asks MCP server for a screenshot of Calculator's window
comments.messages[9].content[0].content[0]: Screenshot of the window; click coordinates use its pixels
comments.messages[9].content[0].content[1]: Path where the harness saved the image
comments.messages[9].content[0].content[2]: Clickable elements from the accessibility API, with their positions
comments.messages[9].content[1]: Harness confirms the todo list update

6.title: Batch of seven clicks
6.text: In this step, the model analyzes the buttons from the accessibility API and the image itself, and decides where to send the clicks.

comments.messages[10].content[0]: Model thinks; the text is not in the log
comments.messages[10].content[1]: Model reads the clear key from the image
comments.messages[10].content[2]: Model asks MCP server for seven clicks and a screenshot in one call
comments.messages[11].content[0]: MCP server returns the results of all eight actions
comments.messages[11].content[0].content[1]: Each click pressed a named button through the accessibility API

comments.messages[12].content[1]: Model asks MCP server to click 5 at the centre of element [14] from the list in call 5
comments.messages[13].content[0]: MCP server reports which button was pressed, without a screenshot
comments.messages[13].content[1]: Harness confirms the todo list update

8.title: Releasing the app
8.text: Claude calls app_release, and the result is "All app locks released."

comments.messages[14].content[0]: Model asks MCP server to release Calculator

9.title: Final reply
9.text: Claude calls wrap_up, a desktop-app tool that can show a next-step box under the chat. Nothing was pending, so the result says no box is drawn and tells Claude to write its closing message. The reply to this request is text with stop_reason: "end_turn", so Claude Code sends no further request. The last request contained 18 messages and both screenshots, about 108k input tokens. From call 3 on, all but a few dozen to about two thousand tokens of each request were read from the prompt cache.

comments.messages[16].content[0]: Model sends a recap to the desktop app; with nothing pending, no box is drawn
comments.messages[17].content[0]: Harness tells the model to write its closing message
comments.response.content[0]: Model's final answer to the user
comments.response.stop_reason: No tool calls, so the loop ends

more: The API keeps no state between calls, so Claude Code sends the whole conversation in every request. Cache breakpoints on the system prompt and on the two newest messages let the API reuse everything up to the end of the previous request. Each bar is one call's input: grey was read from the cache, orange was written to it.
